_comment: klt lvs request document -- the positive control. Both `layout.netlist`
and `reference.netlist` are pre-extracted/hand-authored SPICE files, not
klt lvs's inline-extraction `{file, deck}` shape -- deliberately: inline
extraction hands the comparer a native Python-object netlist on the
layout side (device class name exactly 'nfet', from
ExtractionDeck.nfet_class) against a NetlistSpiceReader-parsed netlist
on the reference side (which upper-cases the model name into its own
device class, 'NFET') -- a real, cosmetic (case-only) class-name split
between the two engines' netlist representations that shows up as a
'topology'-category mismatch even though the design is not actually
wrong. Pointing both sides at pre-extracted/hand-written SPICE files (so
NetlistSpiceReader parses both consistently) avoids this artifact,
which is what makes 'status: match, mismatch_count: 0' a meaningful
positive-control result rather than one polluted by an engine quirk.
See ../../README.md for this bring-up's write-up of the finding.
`layout.netlist` (lvs_unit.spice) is regenerated from lvs_unit.gds by
`klt extract` (see run_lvs.py --regen); `reference.netlist` is
hand-authored. Both paths are relative to THIS file's own directory
(klt lvs resolves request-relative paths against the request
document's location, not the invoking shell's cwd) -- keep this file
in cells/, next to both. Runnable by hand:
klt lvs layout/lvs/cells/lvs_request_match.json --format json
